items.exp: Types: MEN 1, MEN 2A, MEN 2B/MEN 3, MEN 4. (Book p858)

items.q: MEN1 inheritance and sex ratio are:
items.exp: MEN1 is autosomal dominant with M = F. (Book p858)

items.q: MEN1 is caused by mutation of the ___ gene (tumour suppressor) on chromosome 11q.
items.exp: MENIN gene (tumour suppressor) mutation on Chr 11q; d/t intron inversion > base pair deletion. (Book p858)

items.q: The mutation mechanism in MEN1 is typically:
items.exp: D/t intron inversion > base pair deletion. (Book p858)

items.q: Match the MEN1 major ‘3P’ involvement with frequency — 1) Parathyroid  2) Pancreas  3) Pituitary … A) 50–70%  B) 30–50%  C) 100%
items.exp: Major (age <20 yrs) 3P: parathyroid 100%, pancreas 50–70%, pituitary 30–50%. (Book p858)

items.q: The MEN1 minor skin lesions in order are:
items.exp: Skin minor manifestations: angiofibroma > collagenoma > lipoma. (Book p858)

items.q: The m/c benign minor tumour and the m/c neurotumour in MEN1 are respectively:
items.exp: Benign minor tumours: adreno-cortical adenoma (m/c), meningioma (m/c neurotumour), pheochromocytoma (<1%). (Book p858)

items.q: The malignant minor tumours of MEN1 are:
items.exp: Malignant minor: primitive neuro-ectodermal tumour (PNET), thymic & foregut carcinoid. (Book p858)
